name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Alberta
eligibility: Grade 11, north of Red Deer, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Paid 6-week summer research placement in health sciences. Work alongside UofA researchers. ~20 spots from ~175 applicants.

name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Calgary
eligibility: Grade 11, south of Red Deer to north of Claresholm, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Paid summer research in biomedical and health sciences at UCalgary. Cohort programming, guest lectures, poster symposium.

name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Lethbridge
eligibility: Grade 11, in or south of Claresholm, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Paid summer health research at ULethbridge. Guest lectures, panel discussions, poster showcase on Aug 13.

name: WISEST Summer Research Program
eligibility: Grade 11 students; focus on underrepresented groups in STEM, open to all genders
description: 6-week paid STEM research internship. ~40 spots. Lab or field work with UofA researchers. Running since 1984.

name: FEM+ Engineering Mentorship Program
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: Women high school students interested in engineering
description: 7-month mentorship pairing high school students with UofA engineering students. Info sessions and social events included.

name: ELITE Program for Black Youth
eligibility: Black youth aged 15–22 interested in STEM
description: Paid STEM research internship creating experiential learning opportunities for Black youth in science and innovation.

name: TeamUP Science
eligibility: Inner-city, rural, and Indigenous students
description: Alberta-based mentorship and experiential learning for students underrepresented in STEM.

name: SHAD Canada
eligibility: Grades 10–11, strong academics, leadership
description: Month-long STEAM program on a Canadian university campus. Solve real-world problems in teams. Network with like-minded peers.

name: Sanofi Biogenius Canada Competition
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 9-12 interested in life sciences research
description: Students are paired with professional scientist mentors to develop an original research project in life sciences. Projects culminate in a manuscript and poster presentation at regional and national competitions. Top competitors advance to the national Biogenius Challenge.

name: Youreka Canada
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 9-12 interested in citizen science research
description: A 10-week research and mentorship program where students create and contribute to a citizen science project guided by an undergraduate student mentor. Students develop research skills, collect real data, and present findings.

name: RBC Summer Tech Labs
eligibility: Canadian students in grades 11-12 with interest in coding and technology
description: An 8-week paid internship where students collaborate in small teams to build working prototypes solving real RBC business problems. Students use coding languages like JavaScript and React, attend tech talks, and receive mentorship from RBC engineers.

name: VJKF Indigenous Science and Engineering Program
eligibility: Indigenous (First Nation, Métis, and Inuit) high school students in grades 10-12
description: A one-week program where Indigenous high school students conduct research in science and engineering alongside university professors and graduate students. Students explore STEM fields and university life at the U of A campus.

name: Canada-Wide Science Fair (CWSF)
location: National (2026 CWSF hosted in Edmonton, AB)
eligibility: Canadian students in grades 7–12; must first qualify through a regional science fair (e.g., Southeastern Alberta RSF, CYSF)
description: Canada's largest annual youth STEM event where ~400 top students present original independent research projects across all science disciplines. Alberta students qualify through their regional science fair and compete for awards, scholarships, and international placements.

name: iGEM High School Competition
eligibility: High school students worldwide; requires a school or community lab sponsor and a teacher or faculty PI
description: The world's premier synthetic biology competition for students. Teams design, build, and test an original biological engineering project over several months, presenting at the annual Grand Jamboree. Alberta has had teams from Edmonton and Calgary.

name: STEM Fellowship Big Data & AI Challenge
location: National/virtual + in-person finale in Calgary, AB
eligibility: Canadian high school students grades 9–12; teams of up to 5; no coding experience required
description: Teams conduct original open-data and AI research on a real-world theme, producing a peer-reviewed manuscript and presenting at a national conference with a finale in Calgary. Builds research writing, data analysis, and academic communication skills.

name: MindFuel geekStarter
eligibility: Alberta students in grades 7–12; teams form through school or community; all STEM fields welcome including robotics, biotech, ICT
description: Alberta-exclusive project-based STEM innovation program where student teams tackle real-world problems using emerging technologies. Teams receive mentorship and may advance to MindFuel's national Tech Futures Challenge.

name: MindFuel Tech Futures Challenge
location: National (AB, BC, SK, MB, ON, QC, NB), in-person events in Alberta
eligibility: Students in grades 7–12 from participating provinces; self-organized teams
description: National innovation challenge where youth teams design and prototype STEM solutions to real-world problems. Teams receive access to industry mentors, workshops, and MindFuel's Connect2Innovate platform. 13+ years running with 5,000+ alumni.

name: Tate High School Internship Program (HIP)
provider: Department of Computing Science, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students (Grade 11–12) with strong interest in computing; open to all genders
description: Paid 6-week summer internship in UAlberta's Computing Science department. Projects span AI, game development, and machine learning. Students work alongside graduate researchers and faculty.

name: Alberta Innovates Summer Research Studentship – UCalgary
eligibility: Exceptional graduating Grade 12 students with 85%+ average; normally an undergraduate program but open to high-achieving seniors
description: Typically for undergraduates, but high-achieving graduating Grade 12 students (85%+ average) may apply for a paid summer health research position at UCalgary before starting university. Competitive and highly selective.

name: Alberta Innovates Summer Research Studentship – UAlberta
eligibility: Exceptional graduating Grade 12 students with 85%+ average; normally an undergraduate program but open to high-achieving seniors
description: Typically for undergraduates, but high-achieving graduating Grade 12 students (85%+ average) may apply for a paid summer research position at UAlberta before starting university. Competitive and highly selective.

name: STEM Fellowship Research Exploration Program – Edmonton
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12
description: Intensive 5-day spring break research experience hosted in University of Alberta labs. Students are introduced to university-level research methods and academic culture. Distinct from the STEM Fellowship Big Data & AI Challenge.

name: Future Creators – University of Alberta
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering; open to all
description: Free program connecting high school students with UAlberta engineering students for virtual mentorship. Project materials are shipped to participants' homes for hands-on engineering projects guided remotely.

name: Cybermentors – University of Calgary
provider: Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary
eligibility: High school girls/young women interested in science and engineering
description: Program connecting high school girls with women in science and engineering at UCalgary. Fosters research and tech-focused development through mentorship, networking, and industry exposure.

name: Destination Exploration – University of Lethbridge
eligibility: High school students; southern Alberta focus
description: Intensive summer STEM camps and programs at ULethbridge that introduce high school students to university-level research facilities and methodologies. Covers science, technology, and campus life.

name: DiscoverE High School Initiatives – University of Alberta
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering and applied science
description: Suite of specialized summer engineering and science workshops at UAlberta featuring project-based research, prototyping, and hands-on lab experience. Includes multiple programs for various interests and demographics.

name: Alberta Junior Forest Rangers (JFR)
provider: Government of Alberta – Forestry and Parks
eligibility: Ages 16–18, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, physically fit
description: Paid 7-week summer field work experience focusing on environmental science, forestry management, and conservation research. Work in Alberta's forests and wildlands under provincial supervision.

name: WILD Outside – Canadian Wildlife Federation
eligibility: Youth aged 15–18 with interest in conservation and the outdoors
description: Free conservation research and leadership program connecting youth 15–18 with nature through hands-on environmental research and conservation projects. Active programming available in Edmonton and Calgary areas.

name: Let's Talk Science – Space Lab / Tomatosphere
provider: Let's Talk Science / Canadian Space Agency
duration: Varies by initiative (ongoing through school year)
eligibility: Alberta high school students, accessed through their school
description: National citizen science initiatives accessible through Alberta high schools. Space Lab and Tomatosphere allow students to collect and analyze real environmental and spatial data, contributing to actual ongoing scientific research.

name: International Summer School for Young Physicists (ISSYP)
eligibility: Grade 11–12 Canadian and international students; highly competitive selection
description: Highly competitive 2-week fully funded summer school at Perimeter Institute for exceptional Grade 11/12 physics students. Features lectures by world-leading theoretical physicists and hands-on research exposure.

name: Quantum Cryptography School for Young Students (QCSYS)
provider: Institute for Quantum Computing, University of Waterloo
eligibility: Grade 11–12 Canadian students with strong math and physics background
description: Intensive week-long dive into quantum information science and cryptography at IQC, Waterloo. Combines lectures, hands-on labs, and direct interaction with leading quantum computing researchers.

name: Blueprint – University of Toronto
provider: University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering
eligibility: Black high school students in grades 10–11 interested in engineering and applied research
description: Free summer program with year-long engagement for Black high school students in grades 10–11. Builds engineering and applied research skills through mentorship by UofT faculty and senior students.

name: Youth Summer Program (YSP) in Medicine – UofT
provider: University of Toronto, Faculty of Medicine
eligibility: High school students interested in medicine and health research
description: Four-week virtual modules exploring medical research, diagnostics, and human anatomy. Hosted by UofT and available online to students across Canada including Albertans.

name: Calgary/Edmonton Brain Bee
eligibility: Alberta high school students
description: Regional neuroscience knowledge competitions for high school students in Calgary and Edmonton. Winners advance to the national Brain Bee where competitors analyze brain tissue and patient diagnoses. Top finishers represent Canada internationally.

name: Immerse Education Virtual Summer School – Research Track
eligibility: High school students worldwide; tuition fee applies
description: Online academic program where students work directly with university tutors to research and draft a university-level paper. Research tracks available in medicine, computer science, engineering, and more. Builds academic writing and independent research skills.

name: CAP High School Prize Exam
eligibility: Alberta high school students with interest in physics
description: Annual national physics exam where top regional performers earn recognition and networking opportunities with university physics labs. Preparation involves deep independent physics research. Top Alberta students often receive connections to university physics programs.

name: Alberta Envirothon
eligibility: Alberta high school students; teams of 5
description: Hands-on, field-based environmental science competition. Teams study aquatic ecology, forestry, soils, and wildlife, then conduct field research and present solutions to industry professionals. Top Alberta teams advance to the North American Envirothon.

name: Technovation Girls – Alberta
eligibility: Young women and girls aged 13–18
description: Global tech education program where teams of young women identify a community problem, conduct user research, and build a mobile app or AI solution. Alberta participants can work remotely or through local hubs. Teams pitch to a panel of tech industry judges.

name: HOSA Canada – Future Health Professionals
eligibility: Alberta high school students interested in health sciences; students can start a chapter at their own school
description: Canadian branch of Health Occupations Students of America. Students conduct deep research to compete in events spanning biomedical laboratory science, epidemiology, and medical law. Students can form local chapters at their own high schools.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) – Canadian Rockies Region
location: Alberta (Calgary and Edmonton teams; regional events in AB)
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12; join or start a team
description: Rigorous engineering challenge where high school teams design, program, and build industrial-size robots in a 6-week build season. Requires applied research in mechanics, CAD, and control systems. Many Alberta teams compete in the Canadian Rockies regional event.

name: CERN Beamline for Schools (BL4S)
duration: Several months (proposal) + fully-funded experiment trip for winners
stipend: Fully funded trip to particle accelerator for winning teams
eligibility: High school students worldwide; teams of 2–9
description: International physics competition where high school teams research and propose an original particle physics experiment. Winning teams receive a fully-funded trip to CERN or DESY to actually run their experiment alongside professional physicists.

name: Conrad Challenge
eligibility: High school students ages 13–18; teams of 2–5
description: International innovation competition where student teams research and develop science and technology solutions for global issues in Aerospace, Cyber-Technology, Health, and Energy categories. Fully virtual, making it highly accessible to Alberta students.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
stipend: Grand prize: $250,000 scholarship + lab for school
eligibility: Students aged 13–18 worldwide
description: Global science and math research competition. Students research a complex concept in life sciences, physics, or mathematics and translate that research into an engaging explanatory video (max 3 min). Grand prize includes a $250,000 scholarship.

name: Students on Ice (SOI) Foundation Expeditions
eligibility: High school students; highly competitive scholarship selection
description: Fully funded scholarships for high school students to join scientific expeditions to the Arctic or Antarctic. Students conduct hands-on environmental and climate field research alongside polar scientists, Indigenous knowledge holders, and global youth peers.

name: PIMS High School Programs – UAlberta / UCalgary
provider: Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences (PIMS)
eligibility: High school students with strong interest in mathematics
description: Specialized summer math camps, research workshops, and advanced problem-solving seminars hosted in partnership with UAlberta and UCalgary. Exposes students to university-level mathematical research and connects them with professional mathematicians.

name: UCalgary Minds in Motion – High School Programs
eligibility: High school students interested in STEM; Calgary area
description: Specialized multi-week high school programs during the academic year focusing on advanced STEM applications, coding, and engineering design projects using UCalgary's university facilities. Distinct from the elementary-level Minds in Motion camps.

name: APEGA Science Olympics
provider: APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta)
eligibility: Alberta high school students; teams of 4–6
description: Province-wide engineering and geoscience competition where high school teams design innovative solutions to real-world STEM challenges, applying physics and engineering principles under timed conditions. Regional events feed into the provincial finals.

name: Inside Education Youth Summits
eligibility: Alberta high school students; nominated or applied through school
description: Fully-funded regional summits covering themes like Energy, Water, and Agriculture. High school teams attend expert workshops, conduct environmental field research, and develop action plans to implement back in their local communities.

name: CyberTitan – National Cybersecurity Competition
location: Virtual + in-person nationals (open to Alberta teams)
eligibility: Canadian high school students grades 9–12; teams of up to 15
description: Canada's national cybersecurity education initiative. Teams are placed in simulated, real-time cyber defense scenarios where they research vulnerabilities, secure operating systems, and defend networks against attacks. Alberta teams regularly compete at nationals.

name: CanSat Canada Design Challenge
provider: Canadian Aeronautics and Space Institute (CASI) / CanSat Canada
eligibility: Canadian high school students; teams of 4–10
description: National aerospace competition where high school teams design, build, and launch a miniature satellite (the size of a soda can). Requires applied research in physics, coding, and telemetry systems. Teams present technical reports alongside their launches.

name: Canadian Computing Competition (CCC)
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
eligibility: High school students at participating Alberta schools
description: Premier Canadian programming and algorithm design challenge hosted by the University of Waterloo. Students apply advanced computer science and algorithmic research to solve complex problems. Top scorers are invited to the Canadian Computing Olympiad (CCO).

name: Canadian Biology Olympiad (CBO)
eligibility: Canadian high school students; grades 11–12 recommended
description: Premier biology competition for Canadian high schoolers requiring university-level reading, physiological data analysis, and laboratory knowledge. Top-scoring students are selected to represent Canada at the International Biology Olympiad (IBO).

name: Team Canada – Regeneron ISEF
provider: Youth Science Canada / Society for Science
stipend: Travel funded for selected Team Canada members
eligibility: Alberta students who qualify through a regional science fair (e.g., CYSF, SARSF); top projects advance to CWSF, then ISEF selection
description: Students submit independent STEM research for a chance to join Team Canada at the world's largest pre-college science competition. Distinct from the regional science fair track — the ISEF selection process is highly competitive and evaluates original, publication-quality research.

name: The Junior Academy – New York Academy of Sciences
location: Virtual (fully online, open to Alberta students)
eligibility: High school students aged 13–17 worldwide; competitive application
description: Prestigious fully virtual global program. Accepted students join an international peer network and are mentored by STEM professionals to research and design solutions for real global challenges over a 10-week sprint. Certificate awarded upon completion.

name: Pioneer Academics Research Program
location: Virtual (online, open to Alberta students); need-based aid available
eligibility: High school students grades 10–12; competitive application; financial aid available
description: Rigorous virtual research institute for high school students. Accepted students work one-on-one with university professors across disciplines — from neuroscience to computer science — to produce a peer-reviewed research paper over 8 weeks.

name: UAlberta High School Model United Nations (HSMUN)
eligibility: Alberta high school students; teams register through their school
description: One of Alberta's largest academic simulations. Students conduct deep independent research into global policy, economics, and international law, then debate and draft resolutions at a multi-day conference on the UAlberta campus.
